quiz.menu.action: Choose a quiz topic or finish
garden.example.title: Quiz — Garden animals
garden.example.description: Four encounters in the garden, three answers per question, and hints to try again at your own pace.
garden.opening.menu: Which garden animal would you like to discover? Choose a topic with the wheel.
garden.opening.intro: Push open the garden gate! Choose a topic with the wheel and OK, then answer the question. If you get it wrong, you can try again.
garden.opening.farewell: The garden creatures wave goodbye. Press OK to go back to the quiz topics.
garden.tunnels.subject: the tunnels
garden.tunnels.question: A little mound has popped up in the vegetable patch. Who digs tunnels under the garden?
garden.tunnels.feedbackA: Well done! The mole digs through the soil with its wide paws. Turn the wheel to choose another topic.
garden.tunnels.feedbackB: The butterfly flies from flower to flower. Our animal digs underground. Listen to the question again.
garden.tunnels.feedbackC: The blackbird looks for food on top of the ground. Our animal digs tunnels. Try again!
garden.hedgehog.subject: the night walk
garden.hedgehog.question: Something is rustling by the hedge! Which spiny animal looks for food in the garden at night?
garden.hedgehog.feedbackA: The robin has feathers, not spines. Listen carefully to the clue and try another answer.
garden.hedgehog.feedbackB: Well done! The hedgehog comes out mostly at night to look for food. The topic wheel is waiting for you.
garden.hedgehog.feedbackC: The dragonfly has wings and flies mostly during the day. Look for a spiny night walker instead. Try again!
garden.snail.subject: the shell
garden.snail.question: After the shower, a shiny trail crosses the path. Who goes for a walk with a shell on its back?
garden.snail.feedbackA: The ant heads home to its anthill without a shell on its back. Look for the little animal with a shell. Try again!
garden.snail.feedbackB: The slug leaves a shiny trail too, but it has no shell on its back. Listen to the question again.
garden.snail.feedbackC: Well done! The snail can hide inside its shell. Turn the wheel to choose another topic.
garden.pollen.subject: pollen
garden.pollen.question: One flower sways, then another. Who carries pollen while visiting the flowers in the garden?
garden.pollen.feedbackA: Well done! Pollen sticks to the bee and travels from flower to flower. The topic wheel is waiting for you.
garden.pollen.feedbackB: The toad hunts on the ground; it doesn’t visit flowers. Look for a visitor that flies. Try again!
garden.pollen.feedbackC: The earthworm moves through the soil; it doesn’t visit flowers. Listen to the question and try another answer.
castle.example.title: Quiz — Castle trades
castle.example.description: Six workshops to visit, three answers per question, and craftspeople who give hints so you can try again.
castle.opening.menu: Which castle workshop would you like to visit? Choose a trade with the wheel.
castle.opening.intro: Welcome to the castle! With the wheel and OK, choose a trade, then an answer. The craftspeople give you a hint if you get it wrong.
castle.opening.farewell: The craftspeople wave from their workshops. Press OK to go back to the trades wheel.
castle.forge.subject: the forge
castle.forge.question: Ting, ting! The blacksmith lays hot iron on his anvil. Which tool does he use to shape it?
castle.forge.feedbackA: Well done! The blacksmith strikes the iron with his hammer to shape it. Turn the wheel to visit another trade.
castle.forge.feedbackB: A paintbrush is for painting. Here, you need a tool that strikes the iron. Listen to the question again.
castle.forge.feedbackC: A ladle is for serving soup. Look for the tool that strikes the anvil instead. Try again!
castle.bread.subject: the bread dough
castle.bread.question: The baker lets his dough rest under a cloth. Which ingredient will help it rise?
castle.bread.feedbackA: Sand doesn’t go in bread. Look for the ingredient that makes the dough rise. Try again!
castle.bread.feedbackB: Well done! Yeast makes tiny bubbles that help the dough rise. The trades wheel is waiting for you.
castle.bread.feedbackC: Pepper adds flavor, but it doesn’t make the dough rise. Listen to the question again.
castle.seeds.subject: the seedlings
castle.seeds.question: The gardener has just sown seeds in dry soil. What should he give them to help them sprout?
castle.seeds.feedbackA: The bell rings, but the soil stays dry. What do the seeds need? Try again!
castle.seeds.feedbackB: A feather doesn’t make the soil damp. Look for what will help the seeds sprout. Listen to the question again.
castle.seeds.feedbackC: Well done! Water lets the seeds start to sprout. Turn the wheel to visit another trade.
castle.mail.subject: the mail
castle.mail.question: The messenger is getting ready to leave for the neighboring castle. What will he take to deliver written news?
castle.mail.feedbackA: Well done! The letter holds the news the messenger must deliver. The trades wheel is waiting for you.
castle.mail.feedbackB: A brick is for building. Look for the object that holds a written message. Try again!
castle.mail.feedbackC: A broom is for sweeping. The messenger needs news to deliver, not chores to do. Try again!
castle.frame.subject: the roof frame
castle.frame.question: The carpenter is preparing the big beams that will hold up the roof. What material does he use?
castle.frame.feedbackA: Wool is soft and used to make clothes. Look for a strong material for the beams. Try again!
castle.frame.feedbackB: Well done! The carpenter cuts and joins wooden beams. Turn the wheel to visit another trade.
castle.frame.feedbackC: Butter is far too soft to hold up a roof. Listen to the question again and choose another material.
castle.vase.subject: the vase
castle.vase.question: In the potter’s hands, a soft ball turns into a vase. What material does he shape before firing it?
castle.vase.feedbackA: Ice melts when it’s heated. The potter needs a material that hardens in the kiln. Try again!
castle.vase.feedbackB: Leaves can’t be molded into this vase. Listen to the question again.
castle.vase.feedbackC: Well done! The potter shapes the clay, then firing makes it hard. The trades wheel is waiting for you.
rabbit.example.title: Branching story — The gray rabbit
rabbit.example.description: Help Pico find his little bell before the party: three trails, a few tries, and two endings at the mill.
rabbit.opening.menu: Choose a trail with the wheel to help Pico find his little bell.
rabbit.opening.intro: Pico, the gray rabbit, is supposed to start the party by ringing his little bell. It’s gone! You help him find it before evening.
rabbit.trail.choose: Choose where to search on the {{label}} trail
rabbit.trail.followClue: Follow the {{label}} clue to the mill
rabbit.garden.label: vegetable garden
rabbit.garden.title: Explore the vegetable garden.
rabbit.garden.scene: Pico crossed the vegetable garden this morning. In the mud, tiny footprints and webbed ones head off in two directions.
rabbit.garden.outcomeA: The tiny footprints lead to Zoe’s oak tree. A black feather flutters on a branch. The magpie calls out to you.
rabbit.garden.outcomeB: The webbed footprints lead to Gustave the duck. He didn’t see anything. Pico heads back to the garden: “Let’s try the other trail.”
rabbit.garden.clue: Zoe saw Nino the miller pick up something shiny. He went back to the mill. Pico hops up: “Let’s go see him!”
rabbit.magpie.label: magpie
rabbit.magpie.title: Ask Zoe the magpie.
rabbit.magpie.scene: Zoe was watching the garden from her oak tree. She saw a glint near the bridge, then Gustave landing on the pond.
rabbit.magpie.outcomeA: “Nino the miller was holding something that jingled,” says Zoe. He was heading back to the mill with his basket under his arm.
rabbit.magpie.outcomeB: “Gustave? He was sleeping by the pond!” Zoe didn’t see anything around him. Better to ask about what was shining.
rabbit.magpie.clue: Pico recognizes the jingle of his little bell. Maybe Nino put it somewhere safe in his mill. You set off down the path.
rabbit.bridge.label: bridge
rabbit.bridge.title: Search near the bridge.
rabbit.bridge.scene: Pico had stopped on this bridge. Something glints in the river; a bit of blue is poking out on the bank.
rabbit.bridge.choiceA: Look at the glint in the water.
rabbit.bridge.outcomeA: Lea the otter dives down to the glint. It’s a quartz pebble! Pico goes back to the bank to keep searching.
rabbit.bridge.outcomeB: It’s the ribbon from Pico’s collar. Lea joins you: “Nino the miller found a little bell here a while ago.”
rabbit.bridge.clue: “Nino took it to the mill to keep it dry,” says Lea. Pico puts his ribbon back on and leads you there.
rabbit.menu.choose: Choose a trail to find Pico’s little bell
rabbit.mill.meeting: At the mill, a little bell jingles behind the window. Pico stands up on his hind legs: “That’s mine!”
rabbit.mill.gather: Bring the three trails together at Nino’s mill
rabbit.mill.inspect: Nino hung it on the latch so its owner would see it. The window is half open, just above the yard.
rabbit.mill.spot: Spot the little bell hanging on the latch
rabbit.mill.prompt: The window is low, but the mill door is closed. Pico wants his little bell. How can you help him?
rabbit.mill.seekWay: Find a way to give Pico back his little bell
rabbit.rescue.branchChoice: Slide a branch through the opening.
rabbit.rescue.callResult: Nino arrives, smiling. “I found it near the bridge!” He opens the window and gives the little bell back to Pico.
rabbit.rescue.branchResult: You slide a branch through the opening. Pico guides you; the little bell slips down to the end of the stick. He gets it back!
rabbit.rescue.doorResult: The handle turns, but the door is locked. Pico looks at the window: “We need another way.”
rabbit.rescue.choose: Choose how to get the little bell down at the mill
rabbit.ending.nino: To thank him, Pico invites Nino to the party. The miller leads the first dance beside him, to the sound of the little bell. Press OK to play again.
rabbit.ending.friends: Pico dashes off to the party with you. He rings his little bell, and all his friends come running, laughing, to dance. Press OK to play again.
rabbit.ending.openParty: Start the party with the recovered little bell
lighthouse.example.title: Branching story — The lighthouse
lighthouse.example.description: Go with Nora to the lighthouse: three paths, two decisions, and consequences that follow each trip.
lighthouse.opening.menu: Which way does Nora take to the lighthouse? Choose with the wheel.
lighthouse.opening.intro: The lighthouse has gone dark. Nora is bringing a light bulb to Luc, the keeper: her mother’s boat is waiting in the fog. You go with her.
lighthouse.route.arrive: Arrive via {{label}} and help Luc at the lighthouse
lighthouse.route.chooseHelp: After {{label}}, choose how Nora lends a hand
lighthouse.beach.label: the beach
lighthouse.beach.title: Go by the beach.
lighthouse.beach.scene: On the path above the beach, Nora finds a rope near a shelter. “It might come in handy!” Should she take it?
lighthouse.beach.choiceB: Leave the rope in the shelter.
lighthouse.beach.resultA: Nora coils up the rope and carries it to the lighthouse. Luc is waiting for her by the cellar trapdoor, which has swollen in the damp.
lighthouse.beach.resultB: Nora puts the rope back in the shelter, then joins Luc at the lighthouse. He is trying to open a trapdoor swollen with damp.
lighthouse.beach.problem: The cellar trapdoor is stuck. Luc needs to get his tools from down there. Nora shows him the rope: “Shall we try pulling?”
lighthouse.beach.withoutRope: The cellar trapdoor is stuck. Without a rope, Nora can help Luc lift it. His tools are right underneath.
lighthouse.beach.solutionA: Pull the trapdoor with the rope.
lighthouse.beach.consequenceA: Luc ties the rope to the handle. Nora pulls with him; the trapdoor opens. With their tools back, they climb up to the lamp.
lighthouse.beach.consequenceB: Nora holds the trapdoor while Luc lifts it. With their tools back, they climb up to the lamp together.
lighthouse.forest.label: the forest
lighthouse.forest.title: Go through the forest.
lighthouse.forest.scene: Under the pine trees, a sign points to the lighthouse. Ines, the forest ranger, suggests a shortcut through the clearing.
lighthouse.forest.resultA: Nora follows the blue marks on the trees. At the last bend, the lighthouse tower rises above the pines.
lighthouse.forest.resultB: Ines walks with Nora through the clearing. They come out right in front of the lighthouse. “Good luck!” calls the ranger.
lighthouse.forest.problem: At the lighthouse, Luc is feeling his way up the stairs. A shutter is closed; his lantern is waiting on a shelf. How can they light the steps?
lighthouse.forest.consequenceA: Nora lights the lantern Luc hands her. He carries the tools; she lights every step up to the lamp.
lighthouse.forest.consequenceB: Pale daylight comes in through the shutter. Nora can see the steps and climbs up behind Luc, who carries the tools.
lighthouse.port.label: the harbor
lighthouse.port.title: Go by the harbor.
lighthouse.port.scene: At the harbor, Sami is mooring his rowboat. The lighthouse is very close, on the other side of the cove. A footbridge runs along the boats.
lighthouse.port.resultA: Sami rows along the shore and drops Nora off at the lighthouse. “I’ll wait for the beam before I leave the harbor,” he tells her.
lighthouse.port.resultB: The footbridge leads Nora to the lighthouse. She spots her mother’s boat, still out at sea, and hurries on.
lighthouse.port.problem: Luc sets his stepladder in front of the lamp. Nora brings him the new light bulb. How can she lend a hand?
lighthouse.port.consequenceA: Nora takes the bulb out of its box and hands it to Luc. He thanks his young helper and turns to the lamp.
lighthouse.port.consequenceB: Nora holds the stepladder while Luc climbs. He takes the bulb from its box, ready to put it in.
lighthouse.trapdoor.withRope: Check the trapdoor with Nora’s rope
lighthouse.trapdoor.withoutRope: Check the trapdoor without a rope
lighthouse.trapdoor.liftTogether: Without a rope, help Luc lift the trapdoor
lighthouse.menu.choose: Choose Nora’s way to the lighthouse
lighthouse.finale.light: Luc puts in the new bulb and turns the switch. A wide beam cuts through the fog. Nora shouts with joy.
lighthouse.finale.gather: Bring the paths together to relight the lamp with Luc
lighthouse.finale.boats: Out at sea, Nora’s mother sees the signal. Her boat and two others follow the channel into the harbor.
lighthouse.finale.guide: Guide the boats through the lit channel
lighthouse.finale.thanks: Back on the dock, Nora finds her mother. “Your light guided us home!” Press OK to choose another path.
lighthouse.finale.reunite: Meet Nora’s mother on the dock
train.example.title: Quiz and adventures — The explorers’ train
train.example.description: A big wheel of ten stations and an exit, five mini-quizzes and five adventures: every visit leads back to the train.
train.opening.menu: Choo-choo! With the wheel, choose a station, or head back to the depot.
train.opening.intro: All aboard! With the wheel and OK, choose a station, then an answer or an adventure. Every visit brings you back to the train. Ready to go?
train.stars.label: Star
train.stars.title: The Star station.
train.stars.scene: The sky is clear. To guide the train north, which star seems to stay almost still in our sky?
train.stars.outcomeA: Well done! The North Star shows the way north. Climb back on the train: another station is waiting for you.
train.stars.outcomeB: A shooting star only shines for a moment. Look for a star that seems to stay in place. Listen to the question again.
train.clouds.label: Cloud
train.clouds.title: The Cloud station.
train.clouds.scene: The pilot is getting her hot-air balloon ready. To watch the clouds, would you rather go up with her or stay on the ground?
train.clouds.outcomeA: The basket rises above the fields. One cloud looks like a whale! Back on the ground, you return to the train.
train.clouds.outcomeB: Through your binoculars, a cloud looks like a train; the wind blows its engine away. The real train is waiting for the next stop.
train.bees.label: Bee
train.bees.title: The Bee station.
train.bees.scene: There’s buzzing all around the flowers! The bees are gathering nectar. What do they turn it into inside the hive?
train.bees.outcomeA: Flour comes from ground grain. Look for what bees make in their hive. Try again!
train.bees.outcomeB: Well done! Bees turn nectar into honey. The train is waiting: choose another station with the wheel.
train.river.label: River
train.river.title: The River station.
train.river.scene: The little bridge is closed. A ferrywoman calls to you from her boat, and a path leads to another bridge. Which way do you prefer?
train.river.outcomeA: The boat glides between the willows’ reflections. The ferrywoman shows you a silver fish. Then you head back to the train.
train.river.outcomeB: From the other bridge, you see the river winding through the meadows. The walk brings you back to the train.
train.numbers.label: Number
train.numbers.title: The Number station.
train.numbers.scene: Two birds land on the fence. Three more join them. How many birds are perched together?
train.numbers.outcomeA: Well done! Two and three make five. All the birds are here; the train is waiting to take you to another station.
train.numbers.outcomeB: Not quite! Count two birds, then keep going with the three new ones: three, four, five. Listen again and have another try.
train.mill.label: Mill
train.mill.title: The Mill station.
train.mill.scene: The windmill’s sails are turning. The miller is making flour. Would you like to carry grain with him or help him watch the wind?
train.mill.choiceA: Carry a small sack of grain.
train.mill.outcomeA: Together, you bring the grain to the mill. Soon, soft flour fills the sack. The train is waiting for you by the field.
train.mill.outcomeB: The miller’s ribbon flutters in the wind. You show him which way it blows, and he sets the sails. Then you return to the train.
train.seasons.label: Season
train.seasons.title: The Season station.
train.seasons.scene: Yellow and russet leaves swirl around the train. In which season do many trees turn these colors?
train.seasons.outcomeA: In spring, new leaves are usually green. Look for the season of golden leaves. Try again!
train.seasons.outcomeB: Well done! In fall, many leaves change color before they drop. The train is waiting for the next stop.
train.lanterns.label: Lantern
train.lanterns.title: The Lantern station.
train.lanterns.scene: At the lantern festival, the lantern maker offers you two lights for the walk. Which one do you prefer?
train.lanterns.outcomeA: The moon lantern casts circles of light on the path. You cross the festival like a little astronaut, then rejoin the train.
train.lanterns.outcomeB: The fox lantern lights up the festival ribbons. Its shadow seems to dance on the walls! After your walk, the train is waiting for you.
train.sounds.label: Sound
train.sounds.title: The Sound station.
train.sounds.scene: Boom, boom! The musician beats a stretched skin to make her instrument ring out. Which instrument is it?
train.sounds.outcomeA: Well done! The drum’s skin vibrates when you hit it. Climb back on the train and choose your next station.
train.sounds.outcomeB: In a flute, your breath makes the sound. Look for the instrument with a stretched skin. Listen to the question again.
train.orchard.label: Orchard
train.orchard.title: The Orchard station.
train.orchard.scene: Under the apple trees, the gardener is making a snack for the travelers. Would you rather fill the basket or wash the apples?
train.orchard.outcomeA: The gardener picks the apples, and you put them in the basket. The snack will be crunchy! Then you head back to the train.
train.orchard.outcomeB: You roll the apples in the water: their skins shine! The snack is ready, and the train is waiting for the next stop.
train.exit.farewell: The train rolls gently back to the depot. Thanks for the ride! Press OK to go back to the stations.
train.exit.action: Head back to the depot after the trip
train.wheel.choose: Choose one of the ten stations or head back to the depot
